title: Backend can link repeated GPS updates to the same child over time
description: Regular transmission of live GPS coordinates enables the backend to correlate successive location samples with the same child or device, building a persistent movement history and linking visits to home, school, or other sensitive places.
assumptions: The backend receives an account identifier, device identifier, session token, or otherwise stable metadata alongside the GPS updates.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on common LINDDUN Pro linkability decomposition; exact subnode may vary by catalog version.

title: Live GPS coordinates can identify the child or household
description: Precise, frequent location updates may directly or indirectly identify the child by revealing home address, school, daily routines, and unique mobility patterns, even if explicit names are absent from the payload.
assumptions: Coordinates are sufficiently precise and frequent to infer identity from recurring locations or patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability from data content/inference; exact numbering may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Continuous location reporting exposes the child's presence and movements
description: The flow reveals where the child is at specific times and over time, disclosing current presence, routes, and visits to sensitive locations such as home, school, clinics, or places of worship.
assumptions: The backend stores or can observe timestamps together with coordinates.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for sensitive personal data/location disclosure; exact subnode may vary.

title: Collection of continuous live GPS data may exceed what is necessary
description: Sending precise coordinates at regular intervals can constitute excessive collection and processing if the service purpose could be met with less frequent updates, lower precision, or on-device processing.
assumptions: The full precision and reporting frequency are not strictly necessary for every feature supported by the backend.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/data minimization-related node under non-compliance; exact node numbering may differ.

title: Child may be unaware of the extent and frequency of location transmission
description: If the app does not clearly communicate that live GPS coordinates are sent continuously or at regular intervals to the backend, the child may not understand the ongoing collection, retention, and use of their location data.
assumptions: Transparency notices or in-app indicators are incomplete, unclear, or not age-appropriate.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node for insufficient transparency/awareness; exact subnode may vary.

title: Processing a child's live location may violate child-data and consent requirements
description: Regular backend processing of a child's precise geolocation may fail to meet legal obligations such as valid consent/authorization, purpose limitation, retention limits, special protections for children's data, or cross-border transfer requirements.
assumptions: Applicable law imposes heightened requirements for children's precise location data and the system may not fully satisfy them.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact node id depends on the LINDDUN Pro catalog version and applicable legal framing.

title: The child may be unable to later deny or contest transmitted location records
description: Persistent backend records of periodic GPS updates can be used as evidence that the child was at particular places and times, reducing plausible deniability and making it difficult to dispute inferred movements or presence.
assumptions: The backend stores timestamps and location history in a way that can be retrieved or relied upon later.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit repudiation-related privacy node; exact numbering may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Stored location history enables linking of records to the same individual over time
description: Writing each location ping into a persistent location history store creates a longitudinal trail that can be linked across sessions, devices, or identifiers, allowing reconstruction of a person's movements and habits.
assumptions: The store retains a stable user, device, account, or pseudonymous identifier with each ping, or otherwise allows correlation of records over time.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability from persistent records; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Location history records may identify an individual
description: Precise or frequent location pings stored over time can identify a person directly or indirectly, even if explicit identifiers are absent, because home/work patterns and unique mobility traces are often distinctive.
assumptions: Stored pings include precise coordinates, timestamps, or metadata sufficient to single out a person.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability node; exact numbering may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Location history reveals sensitive behavior and whereabouts
description: Persisting each location ping discloses sensitive personal information such as visits to medical facilities, places of worship, political events, or intimate routines, exposing behavior beyond what is necessary for many backend functions.
assumptions: The stored history is accessible to internal services, operators, analysts, or attackers, or may later be repurposed.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for sensitive data in storage; exact node id may vary.

title: Users may be unaware of continuous storage of location pings
description: If the backend writes every location ping to long-term storage without clear notice, users may not realize the extent, frequency, retention, or downstream use of location-history collection.
assumptions: Notice is incomplete, unclear, bundled, or not presented at the time location collection occurs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/unawareness node; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Backend may store more location data than necessary or without valid legal basis
description: Writing every location ping to the history store may exceed data minimization, purpose limitation, retention, or lawful-basis requirements if full-fidelity history is not necessary for the stated service.
assumptions: Applicable privacy obligations require necessity, proportionality, retention limits, transparency, or consent/legal basis for location tracking.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact numbering may vary depending on the LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Users may lack sufficient control over stored location history
description: Once each ping is written to the location history store, users may be unable to access, delete, correct, pause, or selectively limit retention and use of their historical location data.
assumptions: The system does not provide effective user controls or rights handling for stored location history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness/unintervenability-related node for lack of user control; exact node id may differ.

title: Linkability of repeated location pings across time
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine can correlate successive location pings received from the backend and link them to the same user or device over time, enabling reconstruction of movement patterns and behavioral routines.
assumptions: Location pings carry a persistent user, device, session, or pseudonymous identifier, or are otherwise linkable by metadata such as token, account, or network context.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability via correlating records over time.

title: Identifiability of the person behind a location ping
description: Location pings forwarded to the geofencing engine may directly identify a person through account identifiers or indirectly identify them because precise location traces are highly distinctive and can often be tied back to an individual.
assumptions: The flow includes precise coordinates and either direct identifiers or sufficiently granular spatiotemporal data to single out a person.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; identifiability may arise from direct identifiers or quasi-identifying location data.

title: Disclosure of sensitive location and presence information
description: Forwarding raw location pings to the geofencing engine exposes sensitive personal data such as current whereabouts, visits to sensitive places, and inferred presence inside or outside zones. Unauthorized access, logging, or over-broad internal visibility could reveal this information.
assumptions: The engine or its supporting infrastructure stores, logs, or makes the incoming location data accessible beyond the minimum necessary processing path.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node id; exact subnode may differ depending on whether exposure occurs in transit, in logs, or at rest.

title: Disclosure of derived zone-entry and zone-exit events
description: Even if raw coordinates are minimized, the geofencing engine derives entry/exit events that reveal presence at specific places and times. These derived events can disclose habits, workplace/home association, religious or medical visits, or other sensitive inferences.
assumptions: The engine persists or shares geofence match results, alerts, or audit records tied to a user or device.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed estimate for disclosure of derived or inferred personal data.

title: Unawareness of secondary use of location data for geofencing
description: Users may not understand that location pings sent to the backend are forwarded to a separate geofencing component for continuous zone monitoring and alert generation, especially if this processing is not clearly explained in notices or settings.
assumptions: The architecture and purpose of geofencing are not fully transparent to users at collection time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node id; exact node may vary based on whether the issue is hidden recipients, hidden purposes, or opaque processing.

title: Excessive sharing of precise location data beyond necessity
description: The backend may forward full-resolution location pings and persistent identifiers to the geofencing engine even when coarser location, reduced frequency, or short-lived identifiers would suffice to determine zone entry or exit. This can violate data minimization and purpose-limitation expectations.
assumptions: Geofencing decisions could be made with less granular data than what is actually transmitted.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; non-compliance may relate to data minimization, purpose limitation, or proportionality.

title: Processing location data without valid consent or other lawful basis
description: If the backend forwards location pings for geofencing and alerting without a valid lawful basis, or continues doing so after consent withdrawal or opt-out, the flow may be non-compliant with privacy obligations.
assumptions: Geofencing is optional or requires explicit consent in the applicable context, or there are jurisdiction-specific lawful-basis requirements.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id; exact subnode depends on the governing legal basis and consent model.

title: Configured zones can link a child or family to specific sensitive places
description: Zone definitions such as home, school, and a friend's house are strong identifiers of a particular family or child. When the Geofencing & Alert Engine reads these locations from the Family Account & Permissions Store, the data can be used to link events or records to the same household and potentially to real-world identities.
assumptions: The stored zone definitions contain precise addresses, coordinates, labels, or stable identifiers tied to one family account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability of stored location/place data may vary.

title: Zone definitions may reveal identity of the family or child
description: Reading configured places like home and school can directly or indirectly identify the child or household, especially when combined with account context or external knowledge about addresses and schools in the area.
assumptions: The engine or connected components can access account context, labels, or sufficiently precise location data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from data content.

title: Sensitive habits and routines can be inferred from configured geofences
description: The set of configured zones reveals private aspects of daily life, such as where the family lives, where children study, social relationships, and recurring movement patterns. Even without live tracking, the configured places disclose personal information beyond what may be necessary for alerting.
assumptions: Zone labels or coordinates are semantically meaningful and retained in readable form.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of information from location-related configuration data.

title: Geofencing engine may access more location configuration data than necessary
description: If the Geofencing & Alert Engine reads full zone records, historical versions, labels, or all family zones when only a subset is needed, unnecessary disclosure occurs within the system. This increases exposure of sensitive household and child location information.
assumptions: The engine has broad read access to the Family Account Store rather than least-privilege access to only required fields.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended as excessive internal disclosure / overcollection by recipient process.

title: Use of stored family places for geofencing may be insufficiently transparent to users
description: Users may not fully understand that saved addresses and place labels in the Family Account Store are continuously read by the Geofencing & Alert Engine to derive alerts and behavioral inferences. This can create an unawareness risk about how configured location data is used internally.
assumptions: The product does not clearly explain this internal data use at configuration time or in privacy notices.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of transparency/unawareness; exact subtree may differ.

title: Configured zone data may be processed beyond the user's consent or expected purpose
description: Family members may provide home, school, or friend's-house locations expecting alert functionality only, while the Geofencing & Alert Engine could use the same data for analytics, profiling, tuning, or secondary purposes. If such processing exceeds the stated purpose or consent, non-compliance risk arises.
assumptions: Purpose limitation, consent scope, or notice may not explicitly cover all downstream uses by the engine.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for non-compliance related to purpose limitation/consent.

title: Repeated geofence alerts reveal the child's routine and location patterns
description: Arrival/departure notifications sent from the geofencing engine to the parent can expose sensitive behavioral patterns such as home, school, extracurricular schedules, and habitual movements. If intercepted, over-shared, or viewed by unintended recipients, these alerts disclose location-related personal information about the child.
assumptions: Notifications contain at least zone identity, event type (enter/exit), and timestamp, and may be visible on lock screens or shared devices.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on information disclosure of location/event data; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Geofence event notifications enable linkability of multiple child activities
description: A sequence of arrival/departure alerts can be linked together over time to build a coherent profile of the same child across zones and times. Even if each alert is individually limited, the stream of notifications allows correlation of events into a detailed movement history.
assumptions: The parent app/account receives multiple alerts tied to the same child or device over time.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability via correlated event records.

title: Notifications make the child detectable at specific places and times
description: The alert itself signals that the child was present at or departed from a particular geofenced zone at a specific time. Anyone with access to the notification channel or device can detect the child's presence or absence at meaningful locations.
assumptions: Notifications are delivered through channels that may be observable by others, such as push notifications, shared devices, or compromised accounts.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability of presence/location events; exact subtree may differ.

title: Parent may be unaware of the precision, frequency, or context of geofence alerts
description: If the notification does not clearly explain what triggered it, how accurate the geofence determination is, or whether delays/errors are possible, the parent may misinterpret the event. Lack of transparency about alert semantics can lead to incorrect assumptions about the child's exact location or timing.
assumptions: The system may send concise notifications without explanatory context on confidence, timing, or geofence boundaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient user awareness/transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Geofence alerts about a child may be sent without valid consent or beyond agreed purposes
description: Sending arrival/departure notifications to the parent may exceed the scope of consent or legal authorization if the child, guardian arrangement, or applicable policy does not permit this level of monitoring or sharing. The flow may therefore violate consent, purpose limitation, or child-privacy expectations.
assumptions: Consent, parental authority, custody arrangements, or policy constraints may limit when and to whom location alerts can be sent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/consent issues; exact subtree depends on the governing compliance basis.

title: Insufficient evidence about alert delivery or acknowledgment can create repudiation issues
description: If the system does not retain adequate records of when a geofence alert was generated, sent, delivered, or viewed, parties may later dispute whether the parent was notified about an arrival/departure event. This can undermine accountability for privacy-relevant disclosures.
assumptions: Audit logging or delivery receipts may be absent or incomplete for notifications.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for repudiation of notification actions; exact subtree may differ.

title: Registration and child-profile data can be linked to an identifiable family
description: The backend receives parent account details together with child name, date of birth, school, and geofence definitions. These attributes can be linked across records and over time to single out and correlate a specific parent-child household.
assumptions: Backend stores or can correlate account identifiers with child profile attributes and geofence data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary by catalog version.

If transport, storage, access control, or logging are inadequate, unauthorized parties could learn intimate details about the child and family.
assumptions: Geofence zones correspond to real-world places relevant to the child; backend persists the data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort disclosure node selection; exact subtree may differ depending on whether the catalog distinguishes data in transit vs at rest.

description: The backend processes children's personal data and inferred sensitive location information. Without an appropriate lawful basis, parental authorization handling, retention limits, security safeguards, and jurisdiction-specific child-privacy compliance, the processing may be non-compliant.

description: The permissions store holds account data together with child profiles and geofence zone data. If records are keyed by stable family or child identifiers, data from different activities and time periods can be linked to build a detailed picture of household composition, routines, and monitored locations.

assumptions: Threat assumes possible weakness in storage-side authorization, isolation, or protection mechanisms.

assumptions: Consent, parental authorization, or another lawful basis may not explicitly cover all stored fields, retention periods, or secondary uses.
